_readme: Human-maintained notes per phase. Everything RENDERED on the map is hard public
record; this file holds the narrative layer plus the live-inventory snapshot.
AVAILABILITY IS NOT RENDERED. Karen: "as of this moment there are x number of
resales listed and x number of lots, but that will certainly change in the next
5 minutes." Baking that into a printed asset guarantees it goes stale, so it is
spoken and dated at record time instead. Run inventory_report.py on record day;
it fills inventory_snapshot here and prints a block to read on camera.
Fields: role, karen_says, note = narrative. karen_lives_here = the Phase 8 flag.
inventory_snapshot = {as_of, resales_listed, new_lots}, written by the tool.

map.data_credit: Phase boundaries & lots: Bay County, FL recorded plats (public record), plat book/page shown per phase
map.disclaimer: Illustrative only — not a survey. Boundaries, homesite counts and street data are public record; for what is actually for sale today, ask Karen.

Phase 1.karen_says: This is where everyone starts — the Sales Center and the model park, not the first homes people bought.
Phase 1.note: Recorded first (plat book 27). Commonly mistaken for the oldest neighborhood.

Phase 2.karen_says: The OGs. First residents in the community bought here.

Phase 3A.note: Phase 3 is three separate recorded plats, not one area.

Phase 3B & 3C.note: 3B and 3C were recorded together on one plat.

Phase 3D.note: Recorded two plat books later than 3A — a separate release.

Phase 5A3.note: NOT skipped. Recorded at plat book 32, page 81 — after Phase 8 — which is why it looks out of sequence.
Phase 5A3.correction: Competitor coverage claims 5A was 'changed and kind of skipped'. Public record says otherwise.

Phase 6B & 6C.note: 6B and 6C were recorded together on one plat.

Phase 8.karen_says: This is my phase — my husband and I live here.

Phase 10.note: Most recently recorded plat in the community (plat book 33, page 98).

karen_first_hand._source: Karen Lawell, resident of Phase 8, 2026-08-19. Her own experience, not a measurement.

hwy79_audible.quote: Phases 1, 2, and 3b & C all could hear 79
hwy79_audible.note: The real noise discriminator. A short, specific list that maps to three recorded plats on the Hwy 79 frontage.

bandshell_audible.quote: you know where the bandshell is, anything within a few miles could hear a loud concert, 6bc, 4a, 3D... and maybe more
bandshell_audible.note: NOT a discriminator between phases -- most of the community hears a loud show sometimes. Never render a hard ring or print a radius: sound varies with event volume, wind, season and tree cover, and Karen is speaking approximately. Keep the "and maybe more" hedge.

scope.note: Area 1 is Phases 1 through 10 — all 16 plats recorded, Phase 10 (PB 33/98) the last of them. Area 2 has no recorded plat yet, so how its phases will be numbered is not public.
scope.verified: Every recorded plat carries AREA 1 in its subdivision name; the distinct AREA values in Bay County record are exactly [1]. Phase 10 is both the highest phase number and the highest plat book/page.
scope.do_not_say: Do not call the next phase "Phase 11" on camera or in writing. The record does not support the name. "Area 2" is the safe term.

second_town_square.contents: unknown — do not speculate about tenants or amenities
second_town_square.timing: a ways out; Area 2 is not recorded yet. Any specific timing is a guess and must be labelled as one.

scope.plat_order_is_not_phase_order: PH 5A3 is PB 32/81 — recorded AFTER Phase 7 (PB 31/14) and Phase 8 (PB 31/71). It is a late infill plat, which is why it has no lot numbers in county data yet. This is also why availability can never be inferred from recording order.
scope.missing_plats: Only PH 5A3 is recorded — there is no 5A1 or 5A2 plat. Ask Karen whether they were replatted or folded into another plat.
